section_1.title: The Familiar Reality: Euclidean Distance
section_1.content: Introduce the standard concept of distance (metric) on a number line. Explain that in our 'normal' world, as numbers get larger (1, 2, 4, 8...), they get further from zero. Establish the concept of convergence: a sum only 'stops' if the pieces being added get smaller and smaller toward zero.
section_1.example: An animation of a rabbit jumping along a number line. In the 'Real' world, jumping 1, then 2, then 4 meters sends the rabbit to infinity. However, jumping 1, then 1/2, then 1/4 keeps the rabbit trapped before the 2-meter mark.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Divisibility Rule (p-adic Valuation)
section_2.content: Introduce the idea that 'closeness' can be defined by divisibility rather than size. Define the 2-adic valuation: the more times a number can be divided by 2, the 'smaller' it is in this new system. Use a visual 'sieve' or 'filter' to show how powers of 2 are processed.
section_2.example: A 'Magic Sorting Machine' where the number 16 (2^4) is squashed into a tiny pebble because it's highly divisible by 2, while the number 3 remains a large boulder because it isn't divisible by 2 at all.

section_3.title: The 2-adic Metric: A New Geometry
section_3.content: Formally define the 2-adic distance: d(x, y) = 1 / (2^n), where 2^n is the highest power of 2 that divides (x - y). Explain that in this world, 2 is closer to 0 than 1 is, and 1024 is practically touching 0. Use a fractal-like visualization to show how the numbers rearrange themselves spatially.
section_3.example: A 'Digital Map' where the distance between 0 and 1024 is visualized as a tiny gap, while the distance between 0 and 1 is a wide canyon.

section_4.title: Convergence Reimagined
section_4.content: Re-examine the divergent series 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... using the 2-adic lens. Since the terms (2^n) are getting 'smaller' (closer to 0) in the 2-adic metric, the series now satisfies the necessary condition for convergence. Contrast the 'divergent' look in Real space with the 'convergent' look in 2-adic space.
section_4.example: Side-by-side animation: On the left (Real World), a tower of blocks grows infinitely high. On the right (2-adic World), each new block added is physically smaller than the last, causing the tower to stabilize at a specific height.

section_5.title: The Sum of All Powers: Calculating -1
section_5.content: Perform the algebraic manipulation of the infinite sum S = 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... Show that S = 1 + 2(1 + 2 + 4 + ...), which simplifies to S = 1 + 2S. Solving for S gives S = -1. Explain that in the 2-adic world, adding all positive powers of 2 actually leads you to the number -1.
section_5.example: A character named 'Digit' the Robot tries to fill a container with bits. By filling it with every power of 2, the container undergoes a 'binary overflow' and clicks over to represent -1, much like how computer integers wrap around.

section_6.title: Conclusion: One Math, Many Metrics
section_6.content: Summarize that 'convergence' isn't a property of the numbers themselves, but a property of the 'ruler' (metric) we use to measure them. Mention that p-adic numbers are essential in modern number theory and cryptography.
section_6.example: A final shot of a person looking through different colored glasses (The 'Real' lens vs. the '2-adic' lens), seeing the same sequence of numbers form two completely different shapes.

section_1.title: The Familiar Reality: Euclidean Distance
section_1.content: Introduce the standard concept of distance (metric) on a number line. Explain that in our 'normal' world, as numbers get larger (1, 2, 4, 8...), they get further from zero. Establish the concept of convergence: a sum only 'stops' if the pieces being added get smaller and smaller toward zero.
section_1.example: An animation of a rabbit jumping along a number line. In the 'Real' world, jumping 1, then 2, then 4 meters sends the rabbit to infinity. However, jumping 1, then 1/2, then 1/4 keeps the rabbit trapped before the 2-meter mark.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Divisibility Rule (p-adic Valuation)
section_2.content: Introduce the idea that 'closeness' can be defined by divisibility rather than size. Define the 2-adic valuation: the more times a number can be divided by 2, the 'smaller' it is in this new system. Use a visual 'sieve' or 'filter' to show how powers of 2 are processed.
section_2.example: A 'Magic Sorting Machine' where the number 16 (2^4) is squashed into a tiny pebble because it's highly divisible by 2, while the number 3 remains a large boulder because it isn't divisible by 2 at all.

section_3.title: The 2-adic Metric: A New Geometry
section_3.content: Formally define the 2-adic distance: d(x, y) = 1 / (2^n), where 2^n is the highest power of 2 that divides (x - y). Explain that in this world, 2 is closer to 0 than 1 is, and 1024 is practically touching 0. Use a fractal-like visualization to show how the numbers rearrange themselves spatially.
section_3.example: A 'Digital Map' where the distance between 0 and 1024 is visualized as a tiny gap, while the distance between 0 and 1 is a wide canyon.

section_4.title: Convergence Reimagined
section_4.content: Re-examine the divergent series 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... using the 2-adic lens. Since the terms (2^n) are getting 'smaller' (closer to 0) in the 2-adic metric, the series now satisfies the necessary condition for convergence. Contrast the 'divergent' look in Real space with the 'convergent' look in 2-adic space.
section_4.example: Side-by-side animation: On the left (Real World), a tower of blocks grows infinitely high. On the right (2-adic World), each new block added is physically smaller than the last, causing the tower to stabilize at a specific height.

section_5.title: The Sum of All Powers: Calculating -1
section_5.content: Perform the algebraic manipulation of the infinite sum S = 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... Show that S = 1 + 2(1 + 2 + 4 + ...), which simplifies to S = 1 + 2S. Solving for S gives S = -1. Explain that in the 2-adic world, adding all positive powers of 2 actually leads you to the number -1.
section_5.example: A character named 'Digit' the Robot tries to fill a container with bits. By filling it with every power of 2, the container undergoes a 'binary overflow' and clicks over to represent -1, much like how computer integers wrap around.

section_6.title: Conclusion: One Math, Many Metrics
section_6.content: Summarize that 'convergence' isn't a property of the numbers themselves, but a property of the 'ruler' (metric) we use to measure them. Mention that p-adic numbers are essential in modern number theory and cryptography.
section_6.example: A final shot of a person looking through different colored glasses (The 'Real' lens vs. the '2-adic' lens), seeing the same sequence of numbers form two completely different shapes.

section_1.title: The Familiar Reality: Euclidean Distance
lecture_lines: On a number line, distance usually depends on size.
Larger jumps like 1, 2, 4 move toward infinity.
Sums only converge if added terms get smaller.
animations: Draw a horizontal number line #FFFFFF. Label 0, 1, 2, 4.
Animate a rabbit jumping from 0 to 1, then to 3, then to 7.
The rabbit continues jumping until it vanishes off-screen right #FF0000.
Reset number line. Rabbit jumps 1, then 0.5, then 0.25.
Animate a vertical dashed line #00FF00 at 2.0 as the rabbit's limit.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Divisibility Rule (p-adic Valuation)
lecture_lines: In 2-adic math, "closeness" depends on divisibility by 2.
Highly divisible numbers like 16 are considered "small."
Numbers like 3 are "large" because 2 doesn't divide them.
animations: Draw a funnel-like machine labeled '2-adic Sieve' #CCCCCC.
Move a large circle labeled '16' #00FF00 into the sieve.
Scale the '16' circle down to 10% size after passing through.
Move a large circle labeled '3' #FF0000 into the sieve.
The '3' circle remains large and bounces off the sieve.

section_3.title: The 2-adic Metric: A New Geometry
lecture_lines: 2-adic distance depends on the highest power of 2 dividing.
Distance d(x, y) equals 1 over 2 raised to n.
Now, 1024 is much closer to 0 than 1.
Numbers rearrange into a surprising, fractal-like geometry.
Large powers of 2 practically touch the origin.
animations: Display the text 'd(x, 0) = 1 / 2^n' #FFFFFF at center top.
Create points 0 #FFFFFF and 1 #FFFF00 with a large gap.
Create point 2 #00FF00 halfway between 0 and 1.
Create point 1024 #00FFFF extremely close to 0.
Transform the points into a branching tree-like fractal #555555.

section_4.title: Convergence Reimagined
lecture_lines: Consider the series: 1 plus 2 plus 4 plus 8.
In real space, this sum clearly diverges to infinity.
But 2-adic terms get smaller as powers of 2 increase.
The series now satisfies the main condition for convergence.
Watch the 2-adic tower stabilize while the real tower grows.
animations: Show '1 + 2 + 4 + 8 +...' #FFFFFF at top.
Create a 'Real World' box #FF0000 on the left. Inside, stack squares of side 1, 2, 4, 8 vertically.
Create a '2-adic World' box #00FF00 on the right. Inside, stack squares of side 1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125 vertically.

section_5.title: The Sum of All Powers: Calculating -1
lecture_lines: Let S be the sum 1 plus 2 plus 4.
We can write S as 1 plus 2 times S.
Solving for S gives the result: S equals negative 1.
Infinite positive sums can equal a negative number here.
This mirrors binary overflow in a computer's memory.
animations: Display 'S = 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 +...' #FFFFFF.
Group '2 + 4 + 8 +...' and transform it into '2(1 + 2 + 4 +...)' #FFFF00.
Replace the inner sum with 'S' to show 'S = 1 + 2S' and solve for 'S = -1' #00FF00.

section_6.title: Conclusion: One Math, Many Metrics
lecture_lines: Convergence depends on the "ruler" used to measure distance.
Different metrics reveal different structures within the same numbers.
These "p-adic" systems are vital for modern cryptography.
animations: Show a pair of glasses in the center.
Through the left lens #FF0000, show the sequence 1, 2, 4 diverging.
Through the right lens #00FF00, show the sequence 1, 2, 4 converging.
Display 'One Math, Many Metrics' #FFFFFF in large font.

outline.title: The 2-adic Metric: A New Geometry
outline.content: Formally define the 2-adic distance: d(x, y) = 1 / (2^n), where 2^n is the highest power of 2 that divides (x - y). Explain that in this world, 2 is closer to 0 than 1 is, and 1024 is practically touching 0. Use a fractal-like visualization to show how the numbers rearrange themselves spatially.
outline.example: A 'Digital Map' where the distance between 0 and 1024 is visualized as a tiny gap, while the distance between 0 and 1 is a wide canyon.

storyboard.title: The 2-adic Metric: A New Geometry
lecture_lines: 2-adic distance depends on the highest power of 2 dividing.
Distance d(x, y) equals 1 over 2 raised to n.
Now, 1024 is much closer to 0 than 1.
Numbers rearrange into a surprising, fractal-like geometry.
Large powers of 2 practically touch the origin.
animations: Display the text 'd(x, 0) = 1 / 2^n' #FFFFFF at center top.
Create points 0 #FFFFFF and 1 #FFFF00 with a large gap.
Create point 2 #00FF00 halfway between 0 and 1.
Create point 1024 #00FFFF extremely close to 0.
Transform the points into a branching tree-like fractal #555555.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):

        self.setup_layout(
            "Conclusion: One Math, Many Metrics",

                "Convergence depends on the \"ruler\" used to measure distance.",
                "Different metrics reveal different structures within the same numbers.",
                "These \"p-adic\" systems are vital for modern cryptography."

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a pair of glasses in the center.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        left_lens = Circle(radius=0.8, color=WHITE)
        right_lens = Circle(radius=0.8, color=WHITE)

        glasses = VGroup(left_lens, right_lens, bridge).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(glasses, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(glasses))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Through the left lens #FF0000, show the sequence 1, 2, 4 diverging.
        # Through the right lens #00FF00, show the sequence 1, 2, 4 converging.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        
        # Highlight lenses with colors
        self.play(
            left_lens.animate.set_stroke(color="#FF0000", width=8),
            right_lens.animate.set_stroke(color="#00FF00", width=8)

        # Diverging sequence (Left Lens)
        # Positions inside left lens
        div_seq = VGroup(
            Text("1", font_size=20),
            Text("2", font_size=25),
            Text("4", font_size=35),
            Text("8", font_size=45)

            Text("1", font_size=45),

        conv_seq.move_to(right_lens.get_center())

            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display 'One Math, Many Metrics' #FFFFFF in large font.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        final_text = Text("One Math,\nMany Metrics", font_size=36, color=WHITE, t2c={"One Math": YELLOW, "Many Metrics": BLUE})
        self.place_in_area(final_text, "E2", "F5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(glasses),
            FadeOut(div_seq),
            FadeOut(conv_seq),
            Write(final_text)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "In 2-adic math, \"closeness\" depends on divisibility by 2.",
            "Highly divisible numbers like 16 are considered \"small.\"",
            "Numbers like 3 are \"large\" because 2 doesn't divide them."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Divisibility Rule (p-adic Valuation)", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Draw a funnel-like machine labeled '2-adic Sieve' #CCCCCC.
        funnel_outline = VMobject(color="#CCCCCC")
        funnel_outline.set_points_as_corners([
            [-0.7, 0.8, 0], [-0.2, -0.3, 0], [-0.2, -0.8, 0],
            [0.2, -0.8, 0], [0.2, -0.3, 0], [0.7, 0.8, 0]
        ])
        sieve_label = Text("2-adic Sieve", font_size=20, color="#CCCCCC")
        sieve_machine = VGroup(funnel_outline, sieve_label)
        sieve_label.next_to(funnel_outline, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Place in area C2-E4
        self.place_in_area(sieve_machine, "C2", "E4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(funnel_outline), Write(sieve_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Move a large circle labeled '16' #00FF00 into the sieve.
        circle_16 = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.5)
        label_16 = Text("16", font_size=24, color=WHITE).move_to(circle_16.get_center())
        num_16 = VGroup(circle_16, label_16)
        
        # Start at A3
        self.place_at_grid(num_16, "A3")
        self.play(FadeIn(num_16))
        
        # Move into sieve (C3 area center)
        target_center = self.grid["C3"]
        self.play(num_16.animate.move_to(target_center))
        
        # Scale the '16' circle down to 10% size after passing through.
        # Move to E3
        self.play(
            num_16.animate.scale(0.1).move_to(self.grid["E3"]),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Move a large circle labeled '3' #FF0000 into the sieve.
        circle_3 = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=0.5)
        label_3 = Text("3", font_size=24, color=WHITE).move_to(circle_3.get_center())
        num_3 = VGroup(circle_3, label_3)
        
        # Start at A3
        self.place_at_grid(num_3, "A3")
        self.play(FadeIn(num_3))
        
        # Move towards sieve (C3)
        self.play(num_3.animate.move_to(self.grid["C3"]))
        
        # The '3' circle remains large and bounces off the sieve.
        # Bounces to B5
        self.play(
            num_3.animate.move_to(self.grid["B5"]),
            rate_func=bounce,
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let S be the sum 1 plus 2 plus 4.",
            "We can write S as 1 plus 2 times S.",
            "Solving for S gives the result: S equals negative 1.",
            "Infinite positive sums can equal a negative number here.",
            "This mirrors binary overflow in a computer's memory."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Sum of All Powers: Calculating -1", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'S = 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 +...' #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        eq1 = MathTex("S", "=", "1", "+", "2", "+", "4", "+", "8", "+", "\\dots", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(eq1, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(eq1))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Group '2 + 4 + 8 +...' and transform it into '2(1 + 2 + 4 +...)' #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        eq2 = MathTex("S", "=", "1", "+", "2", "(", "1", "+", "2", "+", "4", "+", "\\dots", ")", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(eq2, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(TransformMatchingShapes(eq1.copy(), eq2))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Replace the inner sum with 'S' to show 'S = 1 + 2S' and solve for 'S = -1' #00FF00.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        eq3 = MathTex("S", "=", "1", "+", "2", "S", color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(eq3, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(TransformMatchingShapes(eq2.copy(), eq3))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Intermediate step: S - 2S = 1
        eq4 = MathTex("S", "-", "2", "S", "=", "1", color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(eq4, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(eq3.copy(), eq4))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Result: S = -1
        eq5 = MathTex("S", "=", "-1", color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(eq5, "F3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(eq4, eq5))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Infinite positive sums can equal a negative number here."
        # No specific animation in storyboard, so we highlight the result.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE) # Or stay white
        self.play(Indicate(eq5))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This mirrors binary overflow in a computer's memory."
        self.lecture[4].set_color(BLUE)
        # Visualizing binary overflow concept: ...1111 = -1
        binary_rep = MathTex("\\dots 1111_2", "=", "-1", color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(binary_rep, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(binary_rep))
        self.wait(3)

        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initializing the layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Familiar Reality: Euclidean Distance",
            [
                "On a number line, distance usually depends on size.",
                "Larger jumps like 1, 2, 4 move toward infinity.",
                "Sums only converge if added terms get smaller."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create NumberLine
        # Map 0 to C1 (x=0.5) and 5 to C6 (x=5.5)
        # Length of grid C1-C6 is 5.0. 
        # To match grid spacing (1.0), length=8 covers 0 to 8 units.
        number_line = NumberLine(
            x_range=[0, 8, 1],
            length=8,
            include_numbers=False,
            color=WHITE
        )
        # Position center at C5 so that n2p(0) aligns with C1.
        # 0 is at -4 relative to center. C1 is at x=0.5. 0.5 + 4 = 4.5. 
        # C5 is at x=4.5.
        self.place_at_grid(number_line, "C5")
        
        # Manual Labels for 0, 1, 2, 4 at Row D
        label0 = Text("0", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label0, "D1")
        label1 = Text("1", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label1, "D2")
        label2 = Text("2", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label2, "D3")
        label4 = Text("4", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label4, "D5")
        
        labels = VGroup(label0, label1, label2, label4)
        
        self.play(Create(number_line))
        self.play(FadeIn(labels))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Rabbit represented by a Red Dot
        rabbit = Dot(color="#FF0000")
        rabbit_pos = ValueTracker(0)
        # Using updater for smooth movement relative to number line
        rabbit.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(number_line.n2p(rabbit_pos.get_value())))
        
        rabbit_label = Text("Rabbit", font_size=16, color="#FF0000")

            "In real space, this sum clearly diverges to infinity.",
            "But 2-adic terms get smaller as powers of 2 increase.",
            "The series now satisfies the main condition for convergence.",
            "Watch the 2-adic tower stabilize while the real tower grows."

        COLOR_RED = "#FF0000"

        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_WHITE)

        ]).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)

        self.place_at_grid(indicator, "F5")

        ]).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)

        ]).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)

        ]).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(adic_squares_new, "C4", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)

            ReplacementTransform(real_squares, real_squares_new),

        )

section_1.title: The Familiar Reality: Euclidean Distance
section_1.content: Introduce the standard concept of distance (metric) on a number line. Explain that in our 'normal' world, as numbers get larger (1, 2, 4, 8...), they get further from zero. Establish the concept of convergence: a sum only 'stops' if the pieces being added get smaller and smaller toward zero.
section_1.example: An animation of a rabbit jumping along a number line. In the 'Real' world, jumping 1, then 2, then 4 meters sends the rabbit to infinity. However, jumping 1, then 1/2, then 1/4 keeps the rabbit trapped before the 2-meter mark.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Divisibility Rule (p-adic Valuation)
section_2.content: Introduce the idea that 'closeness' can be defined by divisibility rather than size. Define the 2-adic valuation: the more times a number can be divided by 2, the 'smaller' it is in this new system. Use a visual 'sieve' or 'filter' to show how powers of 2 are processed.
section_2.example: A 'Magic Sorting Machine' where the number 16 (2^4) is squashed into a tiny pebble because it's highly divisible by 2, while the number 3 remains a large boulder because it isn't divisible by 2 at all.

section_3.title: The 2-adic Metric: A New Geometry
section_3.content: Formally define the 2-adic distance: d(x, y) = 1 / (2^n), where 2^n is the highest power of 2 that divides (x - y). Explain that in this world, 2 is closer to 0 than 1 is, and 1024 is practically touching 0. Use a fractal-like visualization to show how the numbers rearrange themselves spatially.
section_3.example: A 'Digital Map' where the distance between 0 and 1024 is visualized as a tiny gap, while the distance between 0 and 1 is a wide canyon.

section_4.title: Convergence Reimagined
section_4.content: Re-examine the divergent series 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... using the 2-adic lens. Since the terms (2^n) are getting 'smaller' (closer to 0) in the 2-adic metric, the series now satisfies the necessary condition for convergence. Contrast the 'divergent' look in Real space with the 'convergent' look in 2-adic space.
section_4.example: Side-by-side animation: On the left (Real World), a tower of blocks grows infinitely high. On the right (2-adic World), each new block added is physically smaller than the last, causing the tower to stabilize at a specific height.

section_5.title: The Sum of All Powers: Calculating -1
section_5.content: Perform the algebraic manipulation of the infinite sum S = 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... Show that S = 1 + 2(1 + 2 + 4 + ...), which simplifies to S = 1 + 2S. Solving for S gives S = -1. Explain that in the 2-adic world, adding all positive powers of 2 actually leads you to the number -1.
section_5.example: A character named 'Digit' the Robot tries to fill a container with bits. By filling it with every power of 2, the container undergoes a 'binary overflow' and clicks over to represent -1, much like how computer integers wrap around.

section_6.title: Conclusion: One Math, Many Metrics
section_6.content: Summarize that 'convergence' isn't a property of the numbers themselves, but a property of the 'ruler' (metric) we use to measure them. Mention that p-adic numbers are essential in modern number theory and cryptography.
section_6.example: A final shot of a person looking through different colored glasses (The 'Real' lens vs. the '2-adic' lens), seeing the same sequence of numbers form two completely different shapes.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initializing the layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Familiar Reality: Euclidean Distance",
            [
                "On a number line, distance usually depends on size.",
                "Larger jumps like 1, 2, 4 move toward infinity.",
                "Sums only converge if added terms get smaller."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create NumberLine
        # Map 0 to C1 (x=0.5) and 5 to C6 (x=5.5)
        # Length of grid C1-C6 is 5.0. 
        # To match grid spacing (1.0), length=8 covers 0 to 8 units.
        number_line = NumberLine(
            x_range=[0, 8, 1],
            length=8,
            include_numbers=False,
            color=WHITE
        )
        # Position center at C5 so that n2p(0) aligns with C1.
        # 0 is at -4 relative to center. C1 is at x=0.5. 0.5 + 4 = 4.5. 
        # C5 is at x=4.5.
        self.place_at_grid(number_line, "C5")
        
        # Manual Labels for 0, 1, 2, 4 at Row D
        label0 = Text("0", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label0, "D1")
        label1 = Text("1", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label1, "D2")
        label2 = Text("2", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label2, "D3")
        label4 = Text("4", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label4, "D5")
        
        labels = VGroup(label0, label1, label2, label4)
        
        self.play(Create(number_line))
        self.play(FadeIn(labels))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Rabbit represented by a Red Dot
        rabbit = Dot(color="#FF0000")
        rabbit_pos = ValueTracker(0)
        # Using updater for smooth movement relative to number line
        rabbit.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(number_line.n2p(rabbit_pos.get_value())))
        
        rabbit_label = Text("Rabbit", font_size=16, color="#FF0000")
        rabbit_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(rabbit, UP, buff=0.1))
        
        self.add(rabbit, rabbit_label)
        
        # Jumps: 0 -> 1, then to 3 (1+2), then to 7 (3+4)
        for target in [1, 3, 7]:
            self.play(rabbit_pos.animate.set_value(target), run_time=1)
            self.wait(0.2)
        
        # Vanish off-screen right
        self.play(rabbit_pos.animate.set_value(12), run_time=1.5)
        self.remove(rabbit, rabbit_label)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Reset rabbit and show convergence
        rabbit_pos.set_value(0)
        self.add(rabbit, rabbit_label)
        
        # Vertical dashed limit line at 2.0 (Grid Col 3)
        limit_line = DashedLine(
            start=self.grid["B3"],
            end=self.grid["D3"],
            color="#00FF00"
        )
        limit_text = Text("Limit: 2.0", font_size=16, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(limit_text, "A3")
        
        self.play(Create(limit_line), FadeIn(limit_text))
        
        # Rabbit jumps 1, then 0.5, then 0.25
        # Positions: 1, 1.5, 1.75
        for target in [1, 1.5, 1.75]:
            self.play(rabbit_pos.animate.set_value(target), run_time=1)
            self.wait(0.2)
            
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title = "The 2-adic Metric: A New Geometry"
        lecture_lines = [
            "2-adic distance depends on the highest power of 2 dividing.",
            "Distance d(x, y) equals 1 over 2 raised to n.",
            "Now, 1024 is much closer to 0 than 1.",
            "Numbers rearrange into a surprising, fractal-like geometry.",
            "Large powers of 2 practically touch the origin."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors from Animation Description
        color_0 = "#FFFFFF"
        color_1 = "#FFFF00"
        color_2 = "#00FF00"
        color_1024 = "#00FFFF"
        color_fractal = "#555555"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # 2-adic distance depends on the highest power of 2 dividing.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        formula_main = MathTex("d(x, 0) = \\frac{1}{2^n}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula_main, "B3", scale_factor=1.1)
        
        v2_def = MathTex("n = v_2(x)", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(v2_def, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(formula_main))
        self.play(Write(v2_def))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Distance d(x, y) equals 1 over 2 raised to n.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        highlight_box = SurroundingRectangle(formula_main, color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(highlight_box))
        self.play(FadeOut(highlight_box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Now, 1024 is much closer to 0 than 1.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_1024))
        
        # Conceptual number line
        num_line = Line(self.grid["E1"], self.grid["E6"], color=GREY_E)
        
        # 0 Point
        dot_0 = Dot(color=color_0)
        self.place_at_grid(dot_0, "E1")
        label_0 = Text("0", font_size=20, color=color_0).next_to(dot_0, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # 1 Point
        dot_1 = Dot(color=color_1)
        self.place_at_grid(dot_1, "E6")
        label_1 = Text("1", font_size=20, color=color_1).next_to(dot_1, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # 2 Point (Halfway conceptually)
        dot_2 = Dot(color=color_2)
        self.place_at_grid(dot_2, "E4")
        label_2 = Text("2", font_size=20, color=color_2).next_to(dot_2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # 1024 Point (Extremely close to 0)
        dot_1024 = Dot(color=color_1024)
        self.place_at_grid(dot_1024, "E1") # Position at origin for effect
        label_1024 = Text("1024", font_size=20, color=color_1024).next_to(dot_1024, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(num_line))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_0, label_0), FadeIn(dot_1, label_1))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_2, label_2))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_1024, label_1024))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Numbers rearrange into a surprising, fractal-like geometry.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(color_fractal))
        
        # Binary Tree Fractal
        def build_tree(start_pos, depth, length, angle, angle_step):
            if depth == 0:
                return VGroup()
            end_pos = start_pos + np.array([np.cos(angle) * length, np.sin(angle) * length, 0])
            line = Line(start_pos, end_pos, color=color_fractal, stroke_width=2)
            left = build_tree(end_pos, depth - 1, length * 0.7, angle + angle_step, angle_step)
            right = build_tree(end_pos, depth - 1, length * 0.7, angle - angle_step, angle_step)
            return VGroup(line, left, right)

        fractal_root = self.grid["C4"]
        fractal_tree = build_tree(fractal_root, 4, 1.2, -PI/2, PI/4)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(num_line, dot_0, label_0, dot_1, label_1, dot_2, label_2, dot_1024, label_1024, formula_main, v2_def),
            Create(fractal_tree)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Large powers of 2 practically touch the origin.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(color_2))
        
        # Origin Marker
        origin_highlight = Star(n=5, color=color_2, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.2)
        origin_highlight.move_to(fractal_root)
        origin_label = Text("0 (Origin)", font_size=18, color=color_2).next_to(origin_highlight, UP)
        
        # Sequential dots moving towards root
        dots_conv = VGroup()
        for i in range(1, 6):
            p_dot = Dot(radius=0.04, color=color_2)
            # Conceptually placing them closer and closer to origin
            p_dot.move_to(fractal_root + np.array([0, -0.5 * (0.8**i), 0]))
            dots_conv.add(p_dot)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(origin_highlight, origin_label))
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(d) for d in dots_conv], lag_ratio=0.3))
        self.wait(2)

            "In real space, this sum clearly diverges to infinity.",

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let S be the sum 1 plus 2 plus 4.",
            "We can write S as 1 plus 2 times S.",
            "Solving for S gives the result: S equals negative 1.",
            "Infinite positive sums can equal a negative number here.",
            "This mirrors binary overflow in a computer's memory."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Sum of All Powers: Calculating -1", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'S = 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 +...' #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        eq1 = MathTex("S", "=", "1", "+", "2", "+", "4", "+", "8", "+", "\\dots", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(eq1, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(eq1))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Group '2 + 4 + 8 +...' and transform it into '2(1 + 2 + 4 +...)' #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        eq2 = MathTex("S", "=", "1", "+", "2", "(", "1", "+", "2", "+", "4", "+", "\\dots", ")", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(eq2, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(TransformMatchingShapes(eq1.copy(), eq2))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Replace the inner sum with 'S' to show 'S = 1 + 2S' and solve for 'S = -1' #00FF00.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        eq3 = MathTex("S", "=", "1", "+", "2", "S", color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(eq3, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(TransformMatchingShapes(eq2.copy(), eq3))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Intermediate step: S - 2S = 1
        eq4 = MathTex("S", "-", "2", "S", "=", "1", color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(eq4, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(eq3.copy(), eq4))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Result: S = -1
        eq5 = MathTex("S", "=", "-1", color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(eq5, "F3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(eq4, eq5))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Infinite positive sums can equal a negative number here."
        # No specific animation in storyboard, so we highlight the result.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE) # Or stay white
        self.play(Indicate(eq5))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This mirrors binary overflow in a computer's memory."
        self.lecture[4].set_color(BLUE)
        # Visualizing binary overflow concept: ...1111 = -1
        binary_rep = MathTex("\\dots 1111_2", "=", "-1", color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(binary_rep, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(binary_rep))
        self.wait(3)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Conclusion: One Math, Many Metrics",
            [
                "Convergence depends on the \"ruler\" used to measure distance.",
                "Different metrics reveal different structures within the same numbers.",
                "These \"p-adic\" systems are vital for modern cryptography."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a pair of glasses in the center.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        left_lens = Circle(radius=0.8, color=WHITE)
        right_lens = Circle(radius=0.8, color=WHITE)
        bridge = Line(LEFT*0.2, RIGHT*0.2).move_to(ORIGIN)
        
        glasses = VGroup(left_lens, right_lens, bridge).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(glasses, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(glasses))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Through the left lens #FF0000, show the sequence 1, 2, 4 diverging.
        # Through the right lens #00FF00, show the sequence 1, 2, 4 converging.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        
        # Highlight lenses with colors
        self.play(
            left_lens.animate.set_stroke(color="#FF0000", width=8),
            right_lens.animate.set_stroke(color="#00FF00", width=8)
        )

        # Diverging sequence (Left Lens)
        # Positions inside left lens
        div_seq = VGroup(
            Text("1", font_size=20),
            Text("2", font_size=25),
            Text("4", font_size=35),
            Text("8", font_size=45)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        div_seq.move_to(left_lens.get_center())
        
        # Converging sequence (Right Lens)
        conv_seq = VGroup(
            Text("1", font_size=45),
            Text("2", font_size=35),
            Text("4", font_size=25),
            Text("8", font_size=20)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        conv_seq.move_to(right_lens.get_center())

        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[Write(m) for m in div_seq], lag_ratio=0.5),
            LaggedStart(*[Write(m) for m in conv_seq], lag_ratio=0.5),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display 'One Math, Many Metrics' #FFFFFF in large font.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        final_text = Text("One Math,\nMany Metrics", font_size=36, color=WHITE, t2c={"One Math": YELLOW, "Many Metrics": BLUE})
        self.place_in_area(final_text, "E2", "F5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(glasses),
            FadeOut(div_seq),
            FadeOut(conv_seq),
            Write(final_text)
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Sum of All Powers: Calculating -1
outline.content: Perform the algebraic manipulation of the infinite sum S = 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... Show that S = 1 + 2(1 + 2 + 4 + ...), which simplifies to S = 1 + 2S. Solving for S gives S = -1. Explain that in the 2-adic world, adding all positive powers of 2 actually leads you to the number -1.
outline.example: A character named 'Digit' the Robot tries to fill a container with bits. By filling it with every power of 2, the container undergoes a 'binary overflow' and clicks over to represent -1, much like how computer integers wrap around.

outline.title: Conclusion: One Math, Many Metrics
outline.content: Summarize that 'convergence' isn't a property of the numbers themselves, but a property of the 'ruler' (metric) we use to measure them. Mention that p-adic numbers are essential in modern number theory and cryptography.
outline.example: A final shot of a person looking through different colored glasses (The 'Real' lens vs. the '2-adic' lens), seeing the same sequence of numbers form two completely different shapes.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let S be the sum 1 plus 2 plus 4.",
            "We can write S as 1 plus 2 times S.",
            "Solving for S gives the result: S equals negative 1.",
            "Infinite positive sums can equal a negative number here.",
            "This mirrors binary overflow in a computer's memory."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Sum of All Powers: Calculating -1", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'S = 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 +...' #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        eq1 = MathTex("S", "=", "1", "+", "2", "+", "4", "+", "8", "+", "\\dots", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(eq1, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(eq1))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Group '2 + 4 + 8 +...' and transform it into '2(1 + 2 + 4 +...)' #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        eq2 = MathTex("S", "=", "1", "+", "2", "(", "1", "+", "2", "+", "4", "+", "\\dots", ")", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(eq2, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(TransformMatchingShapes(eq1.copy(), eq2))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Replace the inner sum with 'S' to show 'S = 1 + 2S' and solve for 'S = -1' #00FF00.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        eq3 = MathTex("S", "=", "1", "+", "2", "S", color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(eq3, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(TransformMatchingShapes(eq2.copy(), eq3))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Intermediate step: S - 2S = 1
        eq4 = MathTex("S", "-", "2", "S", "=", "1", color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(eq4, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(eq3.copy(), eq4))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Result: S = -1
        eq5 = MathTex("S", "=", "-1", color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(eq5, "F3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(eq4, eq5))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Infinite positive sums can equal a negative number here."
        # No specific animation in storyboard, so we highlight the result.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE) # Or stay white
        self.play(Indicate(eq5))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This mirrors binary overflow in a computer's memory."
        self.lecture[4].set_color(BLUE)
        # Visualizing binary overflow concept: ...1111 = -1
        binary_rep = MathTex("\\dots 1111_2", "=", "-1", color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(binary_rep, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(binary_rep))
        self.wait(3)

        self.setup_layout(

            left_lens.animate.set_stroke(color="#FF0000", width=8),

            Text("2", font_size=25),

            Text("2", font_size=35),
            Text("4", font_size=25),

outline.title: The Familiar Reality: Euclidean Distance
outline.content: Introduce the standard concept of distance (metric) on a number line. Explain that in our 'normal' world, as numbers get larger (1, 2, 4, 8...), they get further from zero. Establish the concept of convergence: a sum only 'stops' if the pieces being added get smaller and smaller toward zero.
outline.example: An animation of a rabbit jumping along a number line. In the 'Real' world, jumping 1, then 2, then 4 meters sends the rabbit to infinity. However, jumping 1, then 1/2, then 1/4 keeps the rabbit trapped before the 2-meter mark.

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initializing the layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Familiar Reality: Euclidean Distance",
            [
                "On a number line, distance usually depends on size.",
                "Larger jumps like 1, 2, 4 move toward infinity.",
                "Sums only converge if added terms get smaller."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create NumberLine
        # Map 0 to C1 (x=0.5) and 5 to C6 (x=5.5)
        # Length of grid C1-C6 is 5.0. 
        # To match grid spacing (1.0), length=8 covers 0 to 8 units.
        number_line = NumberLine(
            x_range=[0, 8, 1],
            length=8,
            include_numbers=False,
            color=WHITE
        )
        # Position center at C5 so that n2p(0) aligns with C1.
        # 0 is at -4 relative to center. C1 is at x=0.5. 0.5 + 4 = 4.5. 
        # C5 is at x=4.5.
        self.place_at_grid(number_line, "C5")
        
        # Manual Labels for 0, 1, 2, 4 at Row D
        label0 = Text("0", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label0, "D1")
        label1 = Text("1", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label1, "D2")
        label2 = Text("2", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label2, "D3")
        label4 = Text("4", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label4, "D5")
        
        labels = VGroup(label0, label1, label2, label4)
        
        self.play(Create(number_line))
        self.play(FadeIn(labels))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Rabbit represented by a Red Dot
        rabbit = Dot(color="#FF0000")
        rabbit_pos = ValueTracker(0)
        # Using updater for smooth movement relative to number line
        rabbit.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(number_line.n2p(rabbit_pos.get_value())))
        
        rabbit_label = Text("Rabbit", font_size=16, color="#FF0000")
        rabbit_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(rabbit, UP, buff=0.1))
        
        self.add(rabbit, rabbit_label)
        
        # Jumps: 0 -> 1, then to 3 (1+2), then to 7 (3+4)
        for target in [1, 3, 7]:
            self.play(rabbit_pos.animate.set_value(target), run_time=1)
            self.wait(0.2)
        
        # Vanish off-screen right
        self.play(rabbit_pos.animate.set_value(12), run_time=1.5)
        self.remove(rabbit, rabbit_label)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Reset rabbit and show convergence
        rabbit_pos.set_value(0)
        self.add(rabbit, rabbit_label)
        
        # Vertical dashed limit line at 2.0 (Grid Col 3)
        limit_line = DashedLine(
            start=self.grid["B3"],
            end=self.grid["D3"],
            color="#00FF00"
        )
        limit_text = Text("Limit: 2.0", font_size=16, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(limit_text, "A3")
        
        self.play(Create(limit_line), FadeIn(limit_text))
        
        # Rabbit jumps 1, then 0.5, then 0.25
        # Positions: 1, 1.5, 1.75
        for target in [1, 1.5, 1.75]:
            self.play(rabbit_pos.animate.set_value(target), run_time=1)
            self.wait(0.2)
            
        self.wait(2)

Large powers of 2 practically touch the origin.

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title = "The 2-adic Metric: A New Geometry"
        lecture_lines = [
            "2-adic distance depends on the highest power of 2 dividing.",
            "Distance d(x, y) equals 1 over 2 raised to n.",
            "Now, 1024 is much closer to 0 than 1.",
            "Numbers rearrange into a surprising, fractal-like geometry.",
            "Large powers of 2 practically touch the origin."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors from Animation Description
        color_0 = "#FFFFFF"
        color_1 = "#FFFF00"
        color_2 = "#00FF00"
        color_1024 = "#00FFFF"
        color_fractal = "#555555"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # 2-adic distance depends on the highest power of 2 dividing.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        formula_main = MathTex("d(x, 0) = \\frac{1}{2^n}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula_main, "B3", scale_factor=1.1)
        
        v2_def = MathTex("n = v_2(x)", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(v2_def, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(formula_main))
        self.play(Write(v2_def))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Distance d(x, y) equals 1 over 2 raised to n.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        highlight_box = SurroundingRectangle(formula_main, color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(highlight_box))
        self.play(FadeOut(highlight_box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Now, 1024 is much closer to 0 than 1.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_1024))
        
        # Conceptual number line
        num_line = Line(self.grid["E1"], self.grid["E6"], color=GREY_E)
        
        # 0 Point
        dot_0 = Dot(color=color_0)
        self.place_at_grid(dot_0, "E1")
        label_0 = Text("0", font_size=20, color=color_0).next_to(dot_0, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # 1 Point
        dot_1 = Dot(color=color_1)
        self.place_at_grid(dot_1, "E6")
        label_1 = Text("1", font_size=20, color=color_1).next_to(dot_1, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # 2 Point (Halfway conceptually)
        dot_2 = Dot(color=color_2)
        self.place_at_grid(dot_2, "E4")
        label_2 = Text("2", font_size=20, color=color_2).next_to(dot_2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # 1024 Point (Extremely close to 0)
        dot_1024 = Dot(color=color_1024)
        self.place_at_grid(dot_1024, "E1") # Position at origin for effect
        label_1024 = Text("1024", font_size=20, color=color_1024).next_to(dot_1024, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(num_line))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_0, label_0), FadeIn(dot_1, label_1))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_2, label_2))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_1024, label_1024))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Numbers rearrange into a surprising, fractal-like geometry.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(color_fractal))
        
        # Binary Tree Fractal
        def build_tree(start_pos, depth, length, angle, angle_step):
            if depth == 0:
                return VGroup()
            end_pos = start_pos + np.array([np.cos(angle) * length, np.sin(angle) * length, 0])
            line = Line(start_pos, end_pos, color=color_fractal, stroke_width=2)
            left = build_tree(end_pos, depth - 1, length * 0.7, angle + angle_step, angle_step)
            right = build_tree(end_pos, depth - 1, length * 0.7, angle - angle_step, angle_step)
            return VGroup(line, left, right)

        fractal_root = self.grid["C4"]
        fractal_tree = build_tree(fractal_root, 4, 1.2, -PI/2, PI/4)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(num_line, dot_0, label_0, dot_1, label_1, dot_2, label_2, dot_1024, label_1024, formula_main, v2_def),
            Create(fractal_tree)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Large powers of 2 practically touch the origin.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(color_2))
        
        # Origin Marker
        origin_highlight = Star(n=5, color=color_2, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.2)
        origin_highlight.move_to(fractal_root)
        origin_label = Text("0 (Origin)", font_size=18, color=color_2).next_to(origin_highlight, UP)
        
        # Sequential dots moving towards root
        dots_conv = VGroup()
        for i in range(1, 6):
            p_dot = Dot(radius=0.04, color=color_2)
            # Conceptually placing them closer and closer to origin
            p_dot.move_to(fractal_root + np.array([0, -0.5 * (0.8**i), 0]))
            dots_conv.add(p_dot)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(origin_highlight, origin_label))
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(d) for d in dots_conv], lag_ratio=0.3))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: Convergence Reimagined
outline.content: Re-examine the divergent series 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... using the 2-adic lens. Since the terms (2^n) are getting 'smaller' (closer to 0) in the 2-adic metric, the series now satisfies the necessary condition for convergence. Contrast the 'divergent' look in Real space with the 'convergent' look in 2-adic space.
outline.example: Side-by-side animation: On the left (Real World), a tower of blocks grows infinitely high. On the right (2-adic World), each new block added is physically smaller than the last, causing the tower to stabilize at a specific height.

lecture_lines: Consider the series: 1 plus 2 plus 4 plus 8.

            ReplacementTransform(real_squares, real_squares_new),
            ReplacementTransform(adic_squares, adic_squares_new),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initializing the layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Familiar Reality: Euclidean Distance",
            [
                "On a number line, distance usually depends on size.",
                "Larger jumps like 1, 2, 4 move toward infinity.",
                "Sums only converge if added terms get smaller."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create NumberLine
        # Fix for Issue 31: Use place_in_area and adjust range to fit.
        # Map 0 to C1 and 4 to C5. Length is 4.
        number_line = NumberLine(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            length=4,
            include_numbers=False,
            color=WHITE
        )
        # Center of C1-C5 is at x=2.5.
        self.place_in_area(number_line, "C1", "C5")
        
        # Manual Labels for 0, 1, 2, 4 at Row D
        label0 = Text("0", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label0, "D1")
        label1 = Text("1", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label1, "D2")
        label2 = Text("2", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label2, "D3")
        label4 = Text("4", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label4, "D5")
        
        labels = VGroup(label0, label1, label2, label4)
        
        self.play(Create(number_line))
        self.play(FadeIn(labels))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Rabbit represented by a Red Dot
        rabbit = Dot(color="#FF0000")
        rabbit_pos = ValueTracker(0)
        # Using updater for smooth movement relative to number line
        rabbit.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(number_line.n2p(rabbit_pos.get_value())))
        
        rabbit_label = Text("Rabbit", font_size=16, color="#FF0000")
        rabbit_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(rabbit, UP, buff=0.1))
        
        self.add(rabbit, rabbit_label)
        
        # Jumps: 0 -> 1, then to 3 (1+2), then to 7 (3+4)
        # Even though line visually ends at 4, n2p works for 7.
        for target in [1, 3, 7]:
            self.play(rabbit_pos.animate.set_value(target), run_time=1)
            self.wait(0.2)
        
        # Vanish off-screen right
        self.play(rabbit_pos.animate.set_value(12), run_time=1.5)
        self.remove(rabbit, rabbit_label)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
